data.cultural_impact: The name Sharvankshaana holds cultural significance in Hindu traditions, especially in Maharashtra, where the goddess Sharvani, also known as Ambabai, is popularly worshipped. The name embodies the power and strength of the goddess, who is believed to protect her devotees, provide wisdom, and bring happiness instantly. It is a revered name in Hindu households and is often given as a daughter's name to invoke blessings of the goddess.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Sharvankshaana represents the divine grace of the goddess who is believed to be present in every moment of our lives. It reminds us of the power of the divine force that can bring instant transformation and enlightenment. The name also signifies wisdom, strength, and the power to overcome challenges that come our way. It encourages us to seek the goddess's blessings in difficult times and trust in her ability to bring happiness and peace into our lives.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Sharvankshaana was a queen of the Satavahana dynasty in the 1st century AD. The name Sharvankshaana carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: An inscription from Amaravati mentions her name.
